title.narrative: Ensuring access to equitable, integrated, life‐sustaining primary and specialized healthcare services for vulnerable populations in northwest Syria while enhancing service delivery and preparedness for the outbreaks. (Envelopes 1 and 2)

description.narrative:
The main goal of this Project is to reduce morbidity and mortality among vulnerable populations inside northwest Syria by maintaining access to SHC services and ensuring access to ICU, skin disease, PHC and Mental Health Supplies. It is planned that the result will be reached by supporting the following Outputs: 1. Supporting specialized care through operational support of Salqin "Save the Soul" MNCH hospital (HeRAMS code G0703109), serving as a key facility covering the needs of people in the district area. Proposed activities are focused on the provision of secondary healthcare and specifically supporting "Safe the Soul" Salqin Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health hospital services which are aiming to contribute significantly to decreasing the morbidity and mortality rates among children in Idlib while maintaining access to SHC services. The services provided by the hospital will play a central role in saving lives of critical children cases and reduce the number of children referrals to Turkey because of its location near the border, the hospital also will provide life-saving interventions to end-stage cases moreover, the hospital specialty and capacity make it able to deal with critical cases Respiratory Failure, Dehydration Shock, RDS, Cardiac failure, Severe bronchiolitis, Severe Asthma, etc.
2. Procure life-saving medicines through its own supply chain unit, including pHC, ICU, and Mental Health kits aiming to support access to life-saving treatment and support medication part for service delivery. Due to the ongoing conflict, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, and Cholera outbreaks in the NWS, the health sector is depleted, including the pharmaceutical side, which faces a critical shortage of medicines and supplies, especially ICU, skin disease treatment, analgesic for after-immunization adverse events aiming to cover the critical gap of immunization program and Mental Health related supplies. The proposed project will contribute to the Health Cluster Objective by providing essential medicines and medical supplies to health facilities based on the needs in coordination with health cluster partners.
Within this project WHO is planning to cover the critical gap in maternal and child, reproductive specialized service delivery and ensure service continuity, while procuring and repositioning inside northwest Syria life-saving medicine and medical supplies.
